item.title: Inside the Seattle clinic that treats tech addiction like heroin, and clients detox for up to 16 weeks | Fortune
item.description: A landmark trial over “addictive” social media design is forcing a legal reckoning over whether tech addiction is real and harmful—even as clients at reSTART describe it as a force that has derailed their lives.

item.title: Say hello to 10 a.m. starts. Mark Cuban says AI will cut your workday by an hour—and you’ll still get paid the same | Fortune
item.description: Imagine clocking off an hour earlier every single day and still taking home the same salary. Billionaire Mark Cuban says it's coming, thanks to AI.

item.title: AI's disruption is a choice, not a forecast | Fortune
item.description: Palantir CEO Alex Karp thinks AI will erode the economic power of "humanities-trained, largely Democratic voters." But that assumes a choice.

item.title: Billionaire OnlyFans founder Leonid Radvinsky dies of cancer at 43 | Fortune
item.description: Radvinsky transformed the porn industry with OnlyFans' subscription-based model after acquiring the company that owns and operates the platform in 2018.

item.title: Kalshi and Polymarket rush to update their policies after realizing that Congress could destroy them | Fortune
item.description: In a statement, a Kalshi spokesperson said the company's new features “further demonstrate our commitment to safe markets.”

item.title: Republican states rush to ban abortion pills as surveys suggest they're spiking in pro-life states | Fortune
item.description: Bills intended to keep out the pills have cleared one chamber in Arizona, Indiana and South Carolina this year.

item.title: Philippine president declares state of emergency due to "imminent danger of a critically low energy supply" | Fortune
item.description: The state of emergency will last a year, as the country already started providing 5,000 pesos (~$83) to taxi drivers and other public transport workers.

item.title: JPMorgan has started monitoring the keystrokes, video calls, and meetings of its junior investment bankers—and they say it's for employee well-being | Fortune
item.description: JPMorgan plans to track junior bankers’ hours as Wall Street steers away from its tough 100-hour workweek “rite of passage.”

item.title: Palantir’s billionaire CEO says only two kinds of people will succeed in the AI era: trade workers — ‘or you’re neurodivergent’ | Fortune
item.description: Billionaire Alex Karp tells Gen Z to skip elite college degrees, as one-fifth of Fortune 500 companies recruit more neurodivergent talent by 2027.

item.title: From 12 hours of video games a day to Big Ten Player of the year: The unlikely rise of Yaxel Lendeborg | Fortune
item.description: Lendeborg’s decision to move from the couch to the court paid off in a big way.
